response:
Using only ZeroWire Companion:

**Why care:** CVE-2026-111497 (“node2shell”) is a Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write that corrupts process memory; exposure extends beyond Node.js to HTTP clients, libraries, and container images. [Zero Wire briefing](https://radar.cloudflare.com/security/zero-wire/node2shell)

**Treat it as urgent:** Companion’s cached CISA catalog lists it in KEV, added October 27, 2026. That updates the briefing’s statement that exploitation was not established. KEV membership does not prove your environment is exposed. [CISA KEV](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog)

**Check first:**

1. Find deployed Brotli decoders and versions, prioritizing untrusted input: inbound compressed requests, server-side fetches, URL previews, proxies, and Next.js remote images. Check Node.js `node:zlib`, middleware, and built-in `fetch`. [Evidence](https://radar.cloudflare.com/security/zero-wire/node2shell)
2. Check Python dependencies: affected `brotli >=1.0.3,<1.2.1` and `brotlicffi >=1.0.3,<1.2.1.0`; first fixes are **1.2.1** and **1.2.1.0**, respectively. [Cached advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35)
3. Verify vendor fixes reached running workloads through rebuild/redeployment. Check WAF enforcement: the documented rules default to **Log**, so their presence alone does not establish blocking. [Evidence](https://radar.cloudflare.com/security/zero-wire/node2shell)
